texts.preamble: Bhola And Another vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 June, 2020 Bench: Ramesh Sinha, Mahesh Chandra Tripathi High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Court No. - 1 Case :- Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. - 5298 of 2020 Petitioner :- Bhola And Another Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others Counsel for Petitioner :- Bhavya Sahai
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the impugned FIR which has been registered for the offences in question particularly for the offence under Section 272 and 273 IPC, specific mechanism has been provided to the Food Safety and Standards Act. In support of his argument, he has drawn our attention towards para no.4 of the writ petition relied upon the case of M/s Pepsico India Holdings (Pvt) Ltd. and another Vs. State of U.P. and others of this Court in Writ Petition Bhola And Another vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 June, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76890873/ 1 No.8254 of 2010. Learned AGA opposed the prayer for quashing of the FIR which discloses the cognizable offence and submitted that the offences for which impugned FIR has been registered is under the Excise Act as well as 467, 468, 471 IPC wherein forgery has also been alleged against the petitioners. The Full Bench of this Court in Ajit Singh @ Muraha v. State of U.P. (2006 (56) ACC 433) reiterated the view taken by the earlier Full Bench in Satya Pal v. State of U.P. (2000 Cr.L.J. 569) after considering the various decisions including State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal (AIR 1992 SC 604) that there can be no interference with the investigation or order staying arrest unless cognizable offence is not ex-facie discernible from the allegations contained in the F.I.R. or there is any statutory restriction operating on the power of the Police to investigate a case.
